content: The Rust borrow checker enforces memory safety at compile time without garbage collection.
fastembed uses the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model producing 384-dimensional vectors.
SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers with a single writer, ideal for read-heavy workloads.
The MCP protocol uses JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio for tool-calling between Claude and servers.
HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) graphs provide fast approximate nearest-neighbor vector search in O(log N) time, making it ideal for low-latency semantic retrieval.
tokio::task::spawn_blocking moves CPU-intensive or blocking I/O off the async reactor thread.
DashMap provides concurrent hash map access without global locks, suitable for registry patterns.
The Memory Palace hierarchy: Palace → Wing → Room → Closet → Drawer organizes memories spatially.
L0 loads identity.txt (~100 tokens) on every request. L1 pre-caches top-15 drawers by importance.
Temporal decay: effective_importance = base * 2^(-age_days/half_life) + accumulated_boost.
FNV-1a hash: offset_basis=14695981039346656037, prime=1099511628211. Used for query normalization.
Palace persistence: palace.json holds metadata, identity.txt holds L0 text, l1_cache.json snapshots top-15 drawers.
OpenRouter provides an OpenAI-compatible API at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions.
Conventional commits: feat, fix, chore, docs, test, refactor, perf. Breaking changes marked with !.
The KG triple schema: subject, predicate, object, valid_from, valid_to, confidence, provenance.
r2d2 connection pools over SQLite; each checkout is a physical connection with WAL mode enabled.
usearch index is saved after every upsert via index.save(path). Capacity auto-doubles when full.
Vector search performance benchmarks: usearch (HNSW) reopen ~10 µs; full cold-start (vector + KG) under 2 ms — well within all latency targets.
The setup wizard discovers Claude Code projects by walking ~/Projects for .claude/ or CLAUDE.md.
RecallLog uses FNV-1a to hash normalized queries, tracks hit/miss counts in analytics.db.
